description: We are a student team passionate about space, science and technology. Participating in NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, we aim to explore real-world challenges using NASA data and creative ideas. Our interests include Python, software development, web technologies and data visualisation. We welcome enthusiastic teammates with skills in coding, AI/ML, Earth science, data analysis, research and graphic design. Let's innovate and build together!
summary: EARTH PULSE is an interactive scientific trend-detection workstation developed by Team NOVAFLUX for the "Be An Earth System Trend Detective!" challenge. While standard weather dashboards only plot raw measurements, EARTH PULSE separates statistically significant multi-decadal climate signals from year-to-year weather noise across 44 years (1981–2024, 528 monthly records) of authentic NASA POWER and MERRA-2 Earth system datasets. Our platform directly answers all four core challenge questions: WHAT is changing (2 m Air Temperature T2M, Max Air Temperature T2M_MAX, Radiative Skin Temperature TS, Bias-Corrected Precipitation PRECTOTCORR, and 2 m Relative Humidity RH2M), WHERE it is changing (contrasting humid tropical monsoon foothills in Pala, Kerala against the arid Thar Desert in Jaisalmer, Rajasthan, plus any coordinate clicked on an interactive 2D/3D Globe GIS), BY HOW MUCH (outlier-resistant Theil–Sen decadal slope with 95% confidence intervals), and WHETHER IT IS SIGNIFICANT (two-sided tie-corrected Mann–Kendall trend test at alpha = 0.05).
details:
WHAT DOES EARTH PULSE DO & HOW DOES IT WORK?

EARTH PULSE empowers students, researchers, and citizens to act as Earth System Trend Detectives. Moving beyond basic line charts, it retrieves and analyzes 44-year (1981–2024) multi-decadal time series from NASA's MERRA-2 assimilation model (served via the NASA POWER API) across five geophysical variables:

1. T2M — 2 m Thermodynamic Air Temperature (°C, Mean)

2. T2M_MAX — 2 m Maximum Daily Air Temperature (°C, Mean)

3. TS — Earth Radiative Skin Temperature (°C, Mean)

4. PRECTOTCORR — Bias-Corrected Total Precipitation (mm, Sum)

5. RH2M — 2 m Relative Humidity (%, Mean)

Scientific & Statistical Architecture:

• De-Seasonalized Temporal Slicing: Running a naive t-test on 528 raw monthly observations is statistically invalid because seasonal monsoon cycles introduce severe autocorrelation. EARTH PULSE slices monthly data into three independent 44-year series: Annual (Jan–Dec, 12-month), Southwest Monsoon (JJAS: Jun–Sep, 4-month), and Pre-Monsoon Summer (MAM: Mar–May, 3-month).

• Exact Calendar-Month Precipitation Conversion: Because NASA POWER serves monthly PRECTOTCORR in mm/day, EARTH PULSE multiplies each monthly rate by the exact number of calendar days in that month (accounting for leap years) before summing seasonal and annual totals in mm.

• Non-Parametric Trend Engine: For every selected region and variable, EARTH PULSE computes the two-sided tie-corrected Mann–Kendall Trend Test (S-statistic, Z-score, Kendall's tau, and exact p-value at alpha = 0.05) and the Theil–Sen Robust Slope Estimator (units/decade) across all 946 pairwise year combinations with ranked 95% confidence intervals. It also overlays Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) linear regression to show how Sen's slope resists extreme outliers such as the 2018 Kerala floods.

• Enforced Physical Guardrails: Clearly distinguishes 2 m thermodynamic air temperature (T2M) from modelled radiative skin temperature (TS), orbital satellite MODIS Land Surface Temperature (LST), and derived spectral indices (NDVI).

WHAT BENEFITS DOES IT HAVE & WHAT IS THE INTENDED IMPACT?

EARTH PULSE proves visually and mathematically why a single global forcing drives asymmetric regional responses:

• In Pala, Kerala (9.71°N, 76.68°E — Humid Tropical Monsoon), high soil moisture, dense vegetation, and monsoon cloud cover partition solar energy into latent heat of evapotranspiration, buffering annual T2M warming to +0.16 °C/decade (95% CI: [+0.13, +0.19], p < 0.0001).

• In Jaisalmer, Rajasthan (26.92°N, 70.91°E — Arid Thar Desert), dry soils channel solar radiation directly into sensible heat flux, accelerating annual T2M warming to +0.30 °C/decade (95% CI: [+0.25, +0.35], p < 0.0001).

• In contrast, Corrected Precipitation (PRECTOTCORR) exhibits high inter-annual variability where p-values exceed 0.05 on annual totals, demonstrating why statistical significance testing is vital before claiming a long-term trend.

HOW IS THE PROJECT CREATIVE & WHAT FACTORS DID OUR TEAM CONSIDER?

• Zero-Dependency 2D & 3D Orthographic Globe GIS Engine: Built from scratch in HTML5 Canvas to render exact 0.5° × 0.625° (~55 km) MERRA-2 grid footprints and geodesic distance arcs without external tile-server failures.

• Scientific Integrity & Guardrails: Explicitly reports spatial resolution limits, WMO 1981–2010 baseline anomalies, TS minus T2M radiative coupling spread, and why statistical significance does not by itself prove physical causation.

• 1-Click Research Reproducibility & Cybersecurity: Exports self-documenting CSV spreadsheets with embedded Mann–Kendall and Theil–Sen metadata headers, protected by strict Content Security Policy (CSP) headers, input sanitization, CSV formula-injection defense, and SHA-256 dataset verification.

TOOLS, CODING LANGUAGES, HARDWARE & SOFTWARE USED

• Languages: Python 3 (standard library urllib, math, statistics, hashlib, ssl), HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript (ES6+)

• Visualization: Custom HTML5 Canvas 2D Equirectangular & 3D Orthographic Globe GIS Engine and HiDPI Interactive Chart Engine

• Styling & Typography: Official NASA Space Apps Brand Guidelines implementation using Tailwind CSS, Fira Sans, Overpass, and JetBrains Mono

• Hosting: Netlify

• SI Acknowledgment: Code scaffolding, UI layout, and documentation formatting were assisted by Super Intelligence (Gemini LLM); all measurements and statistical calculations derive strictly from authentic NASA POWER MERRA-2 datasets.
